_what: EVALUATOR-OWNED verification policy. The receipt may DESCRIBE itself; it may not DECIDE what it must satisfy. Every requirement below is resolved from this file plus the receipt's measurable CONTENT, never from a field the producer chose.
_why: Measured on the reviewed branch: a receipt declaring claim_kind=field_only plus engine_contract.numeric_engine_required=false returned exit 0 / VERIFIED / ledger PASS through the full chain. So did one that simply omitted all engine metadata and asserted a number. Both self-certified. claim_verify issued VERIFIED for all six forged cases without ever consulting engine evidence.
_ownership: In production this file must be unwritable by the producing agent: CODEOWNERS on claimgate_plugin/claim_policy.json plus branch protection. That is NOT yet in force, so today this is a strong default rather than a trust root, and it says so in its own output.

numeric_content_detection._rule: CONTENT-DERIVED, and INVERTED 2026-07-25. EVERY number is a claim by default, including numeric-looking strings. Exemption is EARNED by an exact FULL-PATH match on the short reviewed list below — never by a bare key name. The previous denylist-plus-container design was walked through by fixtures b7/b8/b9 and had the same shape as the path-prefix exclusion that was the cheapest bypass earlier in this work: a NAME cannot establish that a number is not a claim.
numeric_content_detection._exempt_note: Every entry is a full dotted path from the receipt root. Adding one is a reviewed act: it declares that a number at that exact location is bookkeeping, not a measurement. A bare name here would re-open b7.

engine_requirement._rule: A numeric claim REQUIRES witnessed engine execution. There is no producer-supplied exemption. numeric_engine_required in a receipt is recorded as a producer ASSERTION and never honoured as policy.
engine_requirement._omission_note: Missing engine metadata on a numeric claim is PENDING EVIDENCE, never 'pure symbolic/SMT/finite by default'. Silence is not an exemption.
engine_requirement._control_only_note: Owner rule 2026-07-22: CONTAINED numpy is allowed as a downstream satellite. numpy labelled or evidenced as LOAD-BEARING is rejected. Containment is enforced by requiring the load-bearing witness to come from an authoritative engine.

exempt_when._rule: Exemption is a property the EVALUATOR establishes from content, not a claim the producer makes.
exempt_when.no_numeric_content: a receipt carrying no numbers in any claim-bearing container needs no engine
exempt_when.smt_only_with_solver_artifact: a purely logical claim is exempt only when it carries a solver artifact (unsat core / proof log) that the evaluator can re-check

metadata_only_ci._rule: A metadata-only evaluation path may never PASS an engine-bearing numeric claim. Its best outcome is PENDING_EVIDENCE.

engine_witness_contract._rule: Numeric agreement between two engines counts only when EACH engine's leg is independently witnessed. Two matching numbers in one JSON file are one assertion, not two engines.
engine_witness_contract._non_finite_note: NaN == NaN is false in IEEE 754, so a NaN pair reads as zero difference and passes a naive agreement test. Non-finite engine values are rejected outright.
